edition: SPI Napoleon at Waterloo, SECOND EDITION, copyright 1971
what_this_is: DECLARED RULINGS. Where the printed 1971 game contradicts itself or leaves a case undefined, the encoding cannot proceed on a coin-flip and must not silently pick one reading. Each row records the competing printed evidence verbatim, the resolution the gate will enforce, and the AUTHORITY for that resolution - per spec #21, whose ladder is: official errata > tournament/publisher clarification > proven outcome-equivalence > declared umpired. These rows are the input for game.json source_defects; they are not the register itself.

rulings.classification: DEFECT IN THE ORIGINAL PUBLISHED GAME - self-contradiction between two primary printed components of the same 1971 folio
rulings.question: Does a defender in a Woods/Road hex double its Combat Strength, as the Terrain Effects Chart prints, or only a defender in a Town, as the rules text prints?

evidence.terrain_effects_chart_verbatim: Towns &  Woods/Roads - Defending unit DOUBLES its Combat Strength. Combat Strength remains at normal value when units attack from such terrain.
evidence.chart_note: printed as ONE row with a single shared Effect-on-Combat cell and two symbol hexes (town; woods-with-road). Folio and Oliver's independent scan agree exactly, so this is neither a misread nor a redraw artefact.
evidence.rules_text_verbatim: (J.) Units defending in Towns DOUBLE their strength (on defense)
evidence.rules_text_note: page 1 never mentions Woods/Roads in this connection, and follows with a Town-hex arithmetic example.
evidence.worked_examples: SILENT. All 27 printed examples on page 2 were transcribed and machine-replayed; NOT ONE places a defender in a Woods/Road hex. The game never demonstrates its own contradiction, so the examples cannot settle it.
evidence.third_edition: NO HELP. The printed 3rd Ed rules state no defence doubling anywhere (PREP-2 E14) and we hold no printed 3rd Ed TEC; the only one in our possession is a contaminated redraw.

rulings.resolution: FOLLOW THE CHART. A defender in a Town hex OR a Woods/Road hex doubles its Combat Strength. Attacking FROM either terrain confers nothing - that half is stated identically by both sources and is proven by printed examples EX-03/EX-04.
rulings.authority: DECLARED RULING - Bruce, 2026-08-14. Both sources are primary and printed in the same folio, so no documentary ladder separates them; the call is a judgement between equals.
reasoning: the chart is the purpose-built terrain document and the artefact players consult at the table, where the rules-text sentence reads as a summary rather than an enumeration
woods being defensively strong is the coherent design reading
Woods entry is otherwise PROHIBITED, so a Woods/Road hex is the only woods a defender can occupy at all
rulings.blast_radius: 5 hexes of 594. hexgraph_2nd_ed.json terrain kind 'woods_road' - the smallest terrain class on the map. A wrong call here is a real but narrowly bounded incorrectness.
rulings.encoding_note: Fable: the doubling predicate keys on the DEFENDER's hex kind in {town, woods_road}. It must NOT key on the attacker's hex; EX-03 proves an attacker in a Town is not doubled.
rulings.citation: folio p.5 Terrain Effects Chart (French half) vs folio p.1 COMBAT case (J.)

rulings.classification: DEFECT IN THE ORIGINAL PUBLISHED GAME - printed typo
rulings.question: none - no rules effect

evidence.printed_verbatim: The act of placing a Prussian unit on the map extends one Movement Point.
evidence.same_page_correct_form: The Act of exiting from the edge of the map expends one Movement Point.
evidence.note: read at 6x, unambiguous. The meaning is not in doubt; 'expends' is plainly intended.

rulings.resolution: Enforce as 'expends' - placing a Prussian on the map costs one Movement Point.
rulings.authority: PROVEN OUTCOME-EQUIVALENCE - the same page prints the correct construction for the mirror-image action two columns later, and no reading of 'extends' yields a coherent alternative rule.
rulings.our_own_lesson: RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md had SILENTLY NORMALISED this to 'expends'. Corrected 2026-08-14 with a footnote recording the original text. A normalisation that reads as a transcription, inside a document whose purpose is verbatim authority, is the class of error worth naming.

rulings.classification: DEFECT IN THE ORIGINAL PUBLISHED GAME - production/layout defect with a real play consequence
rulings.question: none - the rules are unambiguous; the SHEET is not symmetric

evidence.finding: The two halves of the map sheet are NOT mirrors. The British/Prussian half carries RETREAT AND ADVANCE AS A RESULT OF COMBAT (including DISRUPTION and the optional advance) and no Terrain Effects Chart. The French half carries the Terrain Effects Chart and stops after the result codes.
evidence.duplicated_genuinely: Explanation of Results and the Combat Resolution Table grid are printed twice.
evidence.consequence: A French player consulting only his own half of the sheet is never shown the retreat restrictions, the disruption rule, or the advance option.
evidence.our_record_was_wrong: RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 2 claimed TEC x2 and Retreat-and-Advance x2. Both are x1. Found independently by TWO agents reading different pages.

rulings.resolution: No rules effect - the engine enforces the printed rules regardless of which half they are printed on. Registered because it is a genuine defect in the published component and because it explains why a human player may believe a rule does not exist.
rulings.authority: OBSERVED, two independent readings of the printed sheet.

rulings.status: OPEN - needs a ruling before the retreat code is written
rulings.classification: UNDEFINED CASE / possible editing slip in the ORIGINAL PUBLISHED GAME
rulings.question: May a DISRUPTED (displaced) unit be pushed into a Woods/Road hex? The retreat bar says 'non-Road Woods'; the disruption bar two paragraphs later says bare 'woods'.

evidence.retreat_bar_verbatim: may not retreat into enemy ZOC, off the map, into non-Road Woods, or into enemy-occupied hexes
evidence.disruption_bar_verbatim: The disrupted unit itself may not be forced into Enemy units or Zones of Control or woods.
evidence.asymmetry: the disruption bar also OMITS 'off the map', which the retreat bar includes - so it is either deliberately narrower on one axis and wider on another, or loosely drafted.

options: read 'woods' in the disruption clause as the same 'non-Road Woods' the retreat clause defines, treating the shorthand as elision
read it literally - disruption is strictly barred from ALL woods including Woods/Road, a harsher constraint than retreat
rulings.blast_radius: 5 Woods/Road hexes, and only in the displacement branch. Interacts with NAW2-D4: under Bruce's D4 ruling a Woods/Road hex is defensively favourable, which sharpens the question of whether a unit may be shoved into one.
rulings.citation: folio p.5 RETREAT AND ADVANCE AS A RESULT OF COMBAT, paragraphs 2 and 4

handed_forward: PREP-7 carries NAW2-SD-3 into the coverage matrix as an open cell. Everything else here is settled and encodable.
